criteria.text: Nonblank task search covers BOTH `title` and `notes` on SQLite and Postgres.
criteria.reason: SQLite uses real FTS5 and the Postgres repository query is captured at its database boundary.

criteria.text: Postgres candidate retrieval is index-backed via `tasks.search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', boundQuery)` (or equally safe bound plain-query form), never interpolating user input.
criteria.reason: The repository-boundary test asserts the indexed predicate, placeholder, and bound query value.

criteria.text: SQLite candidate retrieval is index-backed via `tasks_fts MATCH ?`, with safely derived/bound lexical terms; raw FTS syntax from users is not accepted/interpolated. If FTS5 is genuinely unavailable, retain a logged title+notes LIKE fallback rather than failing task listing.
criteria.reason: Real SQLite FTS5, raw-syntax rejection, and the logged unavailable-FTS fallback are covered.

criteria.text: Existing visibility, status, scheduled-before, due-before, overdue, collaborator, and ownership filters still apply before candidates leave the repository.
criteria.reason: Focused repository filter and search-visibility tests pass.

criteria.text: All candidates are final-ranked using shared `scoreDocsBm25(search, tasks.map(title + notes))`, score descending. Equal scores use the existing canonical overdue/date/order/created-at ordering, then id as stable final tie. Native DB rank is NOT public ordering.
criteria.reason: Common-corpus ranking and deterministic tie tests pass.

criteria.text: Blank/whitespace/no search preserves existing no-search behavior and canonical order. Existing bare-array API response shape remains unchanged.
criteria.reason: Whitespace no-search and existing bare-array route tests pass.

criteria.text: Common-corpus fixtures prove title-only, notes-only, multi-token stronger-match ordering, no match, filtering/visibility, deterministic ties, and no-search compatibility.

Dev/prod parity is honest: common candidates get identical BM25 ordering; stemming-edge candidate membership may differ because Postgres English stemming != SQLite FTS5 tokenization. Document/test this rather than forcing parity via scans.
criteria.reason: Final verifier isolated postgres:16 runtime evidence proved weighted TSVECTOR, English stemming, and Bitmap Index Scan; documented SQLite FTS5 tokenizer variance remains intentional.
